subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which economic event of 1929 severely weakened the League of Nations' ability to act in the 1930s?
options: The Wall Street Crash and Depression
questions.explain: The Wall Street Crash of 1929 triggered a global Depression that fuelled aggression and weakened cooperation.

questions.q: On which date did the major British offensive at the Battle of the Somme begin in 1916?
questions.explain: The Battle of the Somme began on 1 July 1916, with nearly 60,000 British casualties on the first day.

questions.q: In which year was the League of Nations established, growing out of the post-war peace settlement?
questions.explain: The League of Nations was established in 1920, though agreed at the 1919 Paris peace conference.

questions.q: What 1915 naval-related event, the sinking of a liner by a U-boat, helped turn US opinion against Germany?
questions.explain: The sinking of the Lusitania in 1915 killed American passengers and shifted US opinion against Germany.

questions.q: By the Treaty of Versailles, which industrial region of Germany was demilitarised?
questions.explain: The Rhineland was demilitarised under Versailles, a restriction Hitler defied in 1936.

questions.q: Which major power refused to join the League of Nations, weakening it from the start?
questions.explain: The US Senate rejected membership, so the League lacked the world's strongest economy from the outset.

questions.q: In which year did the assassination of Franz Ferdinand take place and the First World War break out?
questions.explain: Franz Ferdinand was assassinated in June 1914 and war broke out in August 1914.

questions.q: In which year did Hitler become Chancellor of Germany, beginning a more aggressive foreign policy?
questions.explain: Hitler became Chancellor in January 1933, after which he rearmed and challenged Versailles.

questions.q: What did the secret clauses of the 1939 Nazi-Soviet Pact agree to do with Poland?
options: Make it a neutral buffer state
Hand it to the League of Nations
Divide it between Germany and the USSR
questions.explain: The secret protocol of the Nazi-Soviet Pact divided Poland between Germany and the Soviet Union.

questions.q: Which new weapon was first used by the British at the Battle of the Somme in 1916?
questions.explain: Tanks were first deployed by the British during the Battle of the Somme in 1916.

questions.q: The AQA 'Conflict and tension' topic covering the First World War spans which years?
questions.explain: The AQA specification covers conflict and tension from 1894 to 1918.

questions.q: What weakness in the League's main weapon of economic sanctions was exposed by the Abyssinia crisis?
options: Members were forced to send armies
Sanctions were illegal under the Covenant
Key materials like oil were not effectively banned
Sanctions could only last one month
questions.explain: During the Abyssinia crisis, sanctions failed because oil and the Suez Canal were not denied to Italy.

questions.q: In which year was the Treaty of Versailles signed, formally ending the First World War?
questions.explain: The Treaty of Versailles was signed in 1919, imposing harsh terms on Germany.

questions.q: Which clause of the Treaty of Versailles forced Germany to accept blame for causing the war?
questions.explain: Article 231, the War Guilt Clause, made Germany accept responsibility for the war.

questions.q: Which prime minister returned from Munich in 1938 claiming to have secured 'peace for our time'?
questions.explain: Neville Chamberlain returned from the Munich Agreement declaring he had achieved 'peace for our time'.

questions.q: Hitler's aim of expanding German territory to gain 'living space' in the east was known as what?
questions.explain: Lebensraum, or 'living space', was central to Hitler's aggressive eastern expansion plans.

questions.q: Which gas was first used on a large scale by the Germans at Ypres in 1915?
questions.explain: Chlorine gas was first used en masse at the Second Battle of Ypres in 1915.

questions.q: Roughly how many British soldiers became casualties on the first day of the Somme, 1 July 1916?
questions.explain: Britain suffered around 60,000 casualties on the first day of the Somme, nearly 20,000 of them killed.

questions.q: Germany's resumption of which 1917 policy helped bring the USA into the war?
questions.explain: Unrestricted submarine warfare in 1917, sinking neutral and US shipping, helped draw America into the war.

questions.q: The system of opposing European alliances before 1914 chiefly pitted the Triple Entente against which bloc?
questions.explain: The Triple Entente (Britain, France, Russia) opposed the Triple Alliance (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Italy).

questions.q: In which year did the United States enter the First World War on the side of the Allies?
questions.explain: The USA entered the war in 1917, boosting Allied manpower and resources.

questions.q: Which British policy of giving in to Hitler's demands to avoid war is associated with Neville Chamberlain?
questions.explain: Chamberlain pursued a policy of appeasement, most notably at Munich in 1938.
